observed_gate_scope: Matched instrumented original n1 x5 and candidate n9 x5. Operational p50/p95 thresholds only; no statistical-confidence or global maximum-concurrency claim.
boundary: Native api_request event before wrapped generator invocation, including logging and SDK preparation, not HTTP arrival. Missing candidate warm invocations are bounded by turn start and a source-proven model event. One baseline warm internal side query has finite-process-proven ownership but no native invocation event; its first-model boundary is conservatively between turn start and the first main request.
privacy: Only variant/repeat/index/phase, relative timings, counters, booleans, model configuration and source hashes. No prompts, outputs, tool arguments, credentials, native session/request/response IDs, process IDs or local account paths.

original_strict_harness_recomputed.startup_note: First event includes model/network time; it is not pure CLI startup.

clock_verification.assumption: No unobserved realtime clock excursion between bracketing samples; native timestamps are millisecond quantized.
clock_verification.sample_count_note: sample_count counts clock metadata records, including copies in events from one export batch; distinct_clock_samples deduplicates observations.

internal_side_query_diagnosis.request_emission: Official source suppresses api_request for prompt IDs beginning exactly side-query: while still exporting api_response. The raw unmatched completion is retained.
internal_side_query_diagnosis.process_creation_clock_note: Creation timestamps distinguish process identities only. Their epoch-to-monotonic conversion is not used; sampled_monotonic_ns and wait-before-result source establish ordering.
internal_side_query_diagnosis.bounded_timing_rule: Separate finite processes plus native event time establish warm ownership. The earliest request may precede the first main request, so startup lower is zero and fullwork upper is the entire warm turn. No exact auxiliary request time is claimed.

thresholds.interval_pass_rule: candidate upper quantile / baseline lower quantile <= threshold; fail when candidate lower / baseline upper exceeds threshold. Quantiles use individual turn intervals.

historical_evidence_preserved.interpretation: Earlier matched n6 result remains a separate passing observation; no global maximum is inferred.
Earlier whole-turn pass with stricter post-first-tool failure remains separate.
Both exported calls were cold main/auto-memory; the failed cold/warm assumption remains.
Native profile initialization correctly restarted the process; failed retention assumption remains.
Repeated main pairing and absent warm exporter were validated with actual local tools.

limitations: Native telemetry adds overhead. Both variants use identical logging configuration and unchanged direct model routes; these results do not retroactively promote uninstrumented trials.

Candidate warm has 45 bounded samples and no exported request counts. Baseline has nine native samples and one bounded sample due the intentionally unlogged internal recall invocation. Missing request counts are unknown, not zero.
A symmetric ±1ms native event envelope and observed clock-offset uncertainty are retained. No unobserved realtime excursion between clock samples is assumed.

All248 observed main attempts and their completion tails remain checked. The one internal response is separately retained. No observed main completion is even possibly after its result under the uncertainty envelope.
The original strict warm post-first-tool p95 failure is preserved, independently of the v3 native cold fullwork p50 failure. Whole-turn improvement does not imply either failed gate passed.
Five serial baseline pairs and45 candidate pairs provide operational p50/p95 checks only. Cloud variability, telemetry overhead and finite samples prevent a global maximum-concurrency claim.
